records.finding: The release could not be cut: with no replaces, cmd/shortfall/go.sum can only gain a version's hashes once that version is fetchable, so the same-commit runbook produced a release that failed under goreleaser's GOWORK=off + -mod=readonly, and the guard's root-tag-at-HEAD check forbade the only escape.
records.evidence: `GOWORK=off CGO_ENABLED=0 go build .` in cmd/shortfall with a bumped require and untouched go.sum: 'missing go.sum entry needed to verify package ... is provided by exactly one module'. `go mod tidy` for an untagged version: 'unknown revision'.
records.reason: Release is now two commits: waves 1-2 tag the release commit, the CLI's requires bump and go.sum tidy are their own commit, wave 3 tags that. Verified end to end against the pinned goreleaser: 4/4 binaries, correct archives, checksums.

records.finding: The two-commit repair moved the failure rather than removing it: goreleaser's git pipe runs `git describe --exact-match` against GORELEASER_CURRENT_TAG, so naming the root tag demands it sit at HEAD, which this shape makes impossible. release --clean aborted with ErrWrongRef.
records.evidence: goreleaser v2.18.0 internal/pipe/git/git.go validate(): `git describe --exact-match --tags --match ctx.Git.CurrentTag`. Reproduced: 'git tag v0.2.0 was not made against commit 37376848' with the root tag on the parent commit; green with --skip=validate.
records.reason: Runs with --skip=validate; all three checks that flag costs are made elsewhere (tag existence+reachability in the guard, clean tree via git status --porcelain, semver in the guard). Verified: without the flag goreleaser aborts, with it the pipeline completes and the artifact's deps match its label.

records.finding: The stale-require guard passed green whenever its grep matched nothing — quoted module paths (legal go.mod grammar) and a missing go.mod both passed with every require stale — under a comment asserting no branch could pass having found nothing.
records.evidence: `stale=$(grep -E "$first_party" cmd/shortfall/go.mod | grep -vE ... || true)` — zero matches leaves $stale empty and the step passes; and `echo "X=$(guard)"` exits 0 when the guard exits 1; and snapshot: '• building snapshot... version=adapters/export/cloudwatch/v0.2.0-SNAPSHOT' producing a `shortfall_adapters/` directory.
records.reason: Requires are read with `go mod edit -json`, which normalises quoting; missing file, parse failure, empty parse output and zero first-party requires each fail explicitly. Both original shapes verified failing; covered by scripts/release-guard-test.sh.

records.finding: The workflow_dispatch snapshot — documented as the pre-tag rehearsal — derived its version from `git describe --tags`, which in this tag namespace returns a slash-prefixed adapter tag, so it built archives named as nested directories and validated neither version derivation nor artifact naming.
records.evidence: `stale=$(grep -E "$first_party" cmd/shortfall/go.mod | grep -vE ... || true)` — zero matches leaves $stale empty and the step passes; and `echo "X=$(guard)"` exits 0 when the guard exits 1; and snapshot: '• building snapshot... version=adapters/export/cloudwatch/v0.2.0-SNAPSHOT' producing a `shortfall_adapters/` directory.
records.reason: The snapshot job now names itself after the root module's latest tag. Verified: four correctly named archives plus checksums, where it previously produced a `shortfall_adapters/` directory.

records.finding: Self-found before ship: the workflow consumed the guard as `echo "X=$(guard)"`, which exits 0 when the guard exits 1, so a rejected release would have proceeded with an empty version. The guard and its whole suite were decorative.
records.evidence: `stale=$(grep -E "$first_party" cmd/shortfall/go.mod | grep -vE ... || true)` — zero matches leaves $stale empty and the step passes; and `echo "X=$(guard)"` exits 0 when the guard exits 1; and snapshot: '• building snapshot... version=adapters/export/cloudwatch/v0.2.0-SNAPSHOT' producing a `shortfall_adapters/` directory.
records.reason: Assign first, then echo, under set -e. Verified both ways against the step body lifted out of the workflow: happy path exports the version, rejection exits 1.

records.finding: ~60 lines of new branch-heavy release-guard shell shipped with no automated coverage, in a repo that already tests its shell in CI (scripts/commit-lint-test.sh, wired to the pr-title-lint job). A real jq-handling bug survived because of it.
records.evidence: scripts/commit-lint-test.sh is invoked at .github/workflows/ci.yml as the established pattern; no equivalent existed for the release guard. installTargetsExcluded had no direct test and no existing test would go red if it returned its input unchanged.
records.reason: Extracted to scripts/release-guard.sh with scripts/release-guard-test.sh driving 15 cases, run by a new ci job. Proven non-vacuous: disabling the version check or the replace check turns the suite red.

records.finding: The InstallTargets test's comment claimed third-party replaces were caught. ParseMod recorded only first-party ones, so `replace modernc.org/sqlite => ../x` was invisible and the test passed — while `go install` refuses ANY replace.
records.evidence: Quoted claims contradicted by the tree: 'Every nested go.mod replaces its first-party dependencies' with cmd/shortfall carrying none; '`go install ...@latest` works' while @latest resolves to cmd/shortfall/v0.2.0 whose go.mod carries the replaces; 'both replaced rather than dropped' against goreleaser's CheckDirty using `git status --porcelain`.
records.reason: Mod gains OtherReplaces, parseLine records non-first-party replace paths in both directive forms, the test is renamed TestInstallTargetsCarryNoReplaceAtAll and checks both. Negative control confirms a third-party replace now goes red.

records.finding: CONTRIBUTING said `go install .../cmd/shortfall@latest` works; @latest resolves to the still-broken v0.2.0, contradicting README.md in the same diff.
records.evidence: Quoted claims contradicted by the tree: 'Every nested go.mod replaces its first-party dependencies' with cmd/shortfall carrying none; '`go install ...@latest` works' while @latest resolves to cmd/shortfall/v0.2.0 whose go.mod carries the replaces; 'both replaced rather than dropped' against goreleaser's CheckDirty using `git status --porcelain`.
records.reason: Reworded to 'from v0.3.0 on ... will work' with an explicit 'It does not work yet'. All four docs now agree.

records.finding: The bump step was scoped to cmd/shortfall's three requires, but the tree-wide version-agreement test has no exemption, so bumping only those three turns the core test step red.

records.reason: The runbook now splits the bump correctly: the seventeen replaced modules in the release commit, the CLI in the wave-3 commit; modgraph excludes install targets with a non-vacuity floor, and the release guard closes the gap at release time.

records.finding: '--skip=validate drops two goreleaser checks' undercounts: v2.18.0 honours skips.Validate in the semver pipe too, downgrading a non-semver version to a warning and leaving `prerelease: auto` silently inert.
records.evidence: Quoted claims contradicted by the tree: 'Every nested go.mod replaces its first-party dependencies' with cmd/shortfall carrying none; '`go install ...@latest` works' while @latest resolves to cmd/shortfall/v0.2.0 whose go.mod carries the replaces; 'both replaced rather than dropped' against goreleaser's CheckDirty using `git status --porcelain`.
records.reason: The comment names all three, and the guard rejects a non-semver version outright — with a regression case for it, and one asserting a semver prerelease is still accepted.

records.finding: The root tag's existence was proven only incidentally, because the CLI happens to require the core module by name; if it ever stopped doing so the guard would pass and GitHub would mint the release tag at the default branch head.
records.evidence: `sub="${path#github.com/NightWatchEng/shortfall}"; tag="${sub:+$sub/}$version"` — the root tag is reached only when a require's path equals the prefix. goreleaser internal/client/github.go sets TargetCommitish only when release.target_commitish is configured; it is not.
records.reason: The guard asserts refs/tags/$version directly, before the per-require loop.

records.finding: jq was invoked inside `[ ... ]`, so a jq failure was swallowed and reported as the go.mod carrying replace directives — the same misdiagnosis class an earlier fix was written to remove.
records.evidence: With jq absent from PATH: 'jq: command not found' followed by '::error::cmd/shortfall/go.mod carries replace directives', on a go.mod with zero replaces.
records.reason: Every jq invocation now runs where its exit status survives, with its own diagnostic.

records.finding: The herestring comment claimed a piped `while read` would let the step pass, and then that later iterations would run first; `set -euo pipefail` prevents the first and neither is true.
records.evidence: Quoted claims contradicted by the tree: 'Every nested go.mod replaces its first-party dependencies' with cmd/shortfall carrying none; '`go install ...@latest` works' while @latest resolves to cmd/shortfall/v0.2.0 whose go.mod carries the replaces; 'both replaced rather than dropped' against goreleaser's CheckDirty using `git status --porcelain`.
records.reason: The comment now states the real difference — the loop runs in this shell, so the exit is the script's own rather than the pipeline's status. Verified both forms.

records.reason: Added a three-case table test pinning drop, no-op and empty-result behaviour.

records.finding: The first decision record names goreleaser's monorepo.tag_prefix, which the pinned OSS build rejects, and states a scope the delivered change exceeds.
records.evidence: `goreleaser check` on v2.18.0 with a monorepo block: 'yaml: unmarshal errors: field monorepo not found in type config.Project'. The shard's scope says '.github/workflows/release.yml (the tag filter only)'; the delivered change adds two steps and new scripts.
records.reason: A second decision record supersedes it, naming the real mechanism, the founder's re-decision, and the actual scope. The first is left in place as the record of what was decided when.

records.finding: The pkg.go.dev indexing block hard-codes a version with no bump hook, so run verbatim at the next release it would POST fetches for the previous one.
records.evidence: `curl -sS -X POST "https://pkg.go.dev/fetch/...${m}@v0.2.0"` inside a runbook whose three preceding blocks carry the same literal version (`git tag v0.2.0`, `git tag "$m/v0.2.0"`, `git tag cmd/shortfall/v0.2.0`).
records.reason: Refuted by the cross-examiner, the declared single arbiter: the entire Releases runbook is one worked example with the version substituted line by line, and the three git-tag blocks above it carry the same literal. Treating the fourth as a defect while treating those as templates is not a consistent standard. The genuinely weak property — that the POST could not report its own failure — was filed separately and fixed.

records.finding: The pkg.go.dev POST used `curl -sS ... >/dev/null` with no -f, so an HTTP error was not a curl error and the output was discarded — in the step whose whole purpose is to fix a silent staleness failure.
records.evidence: `curl -sS -X POST "https://pkg.go.dev/fetch/..." >/dev/null` — no -f, so a 4xx is not a curl error, and stdout is discarded.
records.reason: Uses curl -fsS and echoes indexed/FAILED per module path.
